title: Evergreen Bank private deploy compatibility and TF upgrade notes
content:
Context and purpose:

This is a working note for Evergreen Bank's private deployment (VPC + on-prem GPU pool) sizing, Terraform module compatibility constraints, and an upgrade path for the runtime/TF modules. The goal is to capture assumptions, quick back-of-envelope sizing, architecture Q&A, and an actionable TF upgrade checklist that the infra lead (Evergreen) can review with their security and network teams.

Status: draft, internal. Not yet approved by Solutions Eng or Security Ops.

Customer background and constraints:
- Evergreen Bank (regulated financial institution) requires a private control plane in their AWS account with on-prem burst capability to two datacenters for DR.
- Data residency: all logs and KV cache snapshots must remain in customer-managed S3 or NFS (on their VPC/VPN), with audit logs forwarded to their SIEM.
- Approved hardware: A100-80GB (primary), V100-32GB for non-production; strict AMI/firmware baseline required.
- Network: transit gateway with strict egress filter via corporate proxy; limited peering to Redwood control plane for management operations (only over mTLS and restricted CIDR).
- Timeline: proof-of-concept (POC) in 6 weeks, pilot (2 node pool) in 3 months, full roll (8–12 nodes) 6 months.

High-level architecture assumption:
- Control plane: Customer-managed (Redwood Private mode), runs in Evergreen's AWS account in a dedicated management VPC (private subnets only).
- Serving runtime: Deployed in a dedicated GPU VPC per region/availability zone. Each serving instance connects to customer-managed S3 for model artifacts and to a KV store (Redis cluster) in the same VPC for cross-request caching.
- Storage: Model artifacts stored in S3 with lifecycle rules; optionally mirrored to on-prem NFS for DR snapshots.
- Secret management: Integrate with customer KMS for encryption; vault agent container is recommended in EKS nodes.

Sizing (initial recommendation — POC -> pilot -> prod):
- POC (dev): 2 x A100-80GB (1 serving, 1 standby/ops), 32 vCPU, 256GB RAM per control-plane instance, small Redis (3 x r6g.large). Expected steady QPS: 1–2 requests/s, peak 10 qps.
- Pilot (2-node pool): 4 x A100-80GB (2 serving active), per-node local NVMe for KV cache (1TB), 64 vCPU and 512GB RAM for control-plane HA pair (3 instances recommended). Redis: 3 x r6g.xlarge, autoscaling enabled.
- Prod target (8–12 nodes): 10 x A100-80GB serving nodes (support for model sharding and high-throughput batching). Plan for warm standby nodes to satisfy SLA. Control plane: 3 x m6i.8x + 2 x m6i.4x for replicas, Redis cluster with persistence on EBS GP3 encrypted volumes.

Notes on quantization/throughput tradeoffs (customer concern):
- Evergreen expects latency <120ms p95 for short prompts (<=256 tokens). Recommend enabling dynamic batching with a 40ms batch window in pilot. Use 4-bit quantized runtimes for high-throughput models where accuracy tests pass. Maintain a non-quantized fallback model.

Terraform module compatibility notes (current repo state as of PR 478):
- Modules touched: private/control-plane, private/gpu-pool, networking/transit, secrets/vault-connector.
- Breaking changes in upstream module v2.0: renaming of variable model_artifact_bucket -> model_bucket_name and migration of kms_key_id to provider-level config. This will require a plan/terraform state migration script for customers with existing state.
- S3 bucket policy templates now assume AWS Partition variable; Evergreen uses GovCloud-style partitions for some workloads — need to parameterize partition and partition-specific ARNs.
- Module private/gpu-pool lacks an explicit lifecycle rule for local NVMe ephemeral device formatting and driver provisioning. We recommend adding a user_data script snippet and a node-bootstrap DaemonSet in EKS for NVMe formatting and permissioning.
- Current module depends on aws_iam_role with wide permissions for dynamic mount operations; for regulated customers we should add an option to supply a minimal IAM role ARN (customer-managed) and skip module role creation.

Planned TF upgrade steps and rollback strategy:
1) Branch and bump module versions (create evergreen-compat branch). Run a terraform validate/plan in a staging account using a mocked state.
2) Add compatibility layer in modules: accept both model_artifact_bucket and model_bucket_name variables and set deprecation warnings. Add variable aws_partition with default "aws".
3) Implement state migration helper: small script to read old state, map names (model_artifact_bucket->model_bucket_name), and output tfstate patch. Document steps clearly for customer infra team.
4) Apply change in POC account with zero-downtime approach: create new resources alongside existing where possible, then switch references in control-plane config.
5) If plan shows destructive operations, abort and open a PR to add non-destructive alternative.

TF checklist for Evergreen (actionable items):
- [ ] Confirm aws_partition value for all accounts (prod, staging, govcloud).
- [ ] Share customer-managed IAM role ARNs for node bootstrap and S3 access.
- [ ] Decide on KMS key usage vs. Redwood-managed key; add kms_key_id into TF variables if customer-managed.
- [ ] Approve NVMe bootstrap DaemonSet image (signed).
- [ ] Provide IP allowlist for Redwood control-plane endpoints (CIDR).

Operational and security assumptions: known gaps to discuss with Evergreen security
- Audit logs: we assume CloudTrail + S3 + SIEM ingestion; ensure retention policy and tamper-protection.
- Network egress through corporate proxy: some runtime telemetry may be blocked; provide offline telemetry buffer and a push mechanism initiated from control-plane to avoid blocked websockets.
- Vulnerability scanning: customer requires nightly container scans. Need a small gating job in TF to fail deploy if critical CVEs present.

Open questions for customer (to resolve in technical discovery):
- Does Evergreen want model artifacts mirrored to on-prem NFS for strict air-gap requirement, or is S3 in-region acceptable?
- Can they expose the Redis cluster to the serving subnet, or do they require a dedicated transit VPC with peered-only access?
- Are there existing operation runbooks for AMI/firmware baseline we should reference?
- What is the expected token-per-second per user workload (we need sample traffic to refine batch sizing)?

Migration risks and mitigations:
- Risk: TF variable rename causes state drift. Mitigation: run plan in staging account with full tfstate snapshot and a dry-run migration tool.
- Risk: network ACLs block control-plane heartbeats. Mitigation: provide a minimal TCP/443 allowlist and test harness early.
- Risk: quantized model regression. Mitigation: maintain small eval-suite with historical prompt set and auto-compare before canary rollout.

Operational runbook (high-level steps for POC):
1) Provision management VPC and control-plane instances (t1). Validate KMS integration and S3 access.
2) Boot GPU pool nodes with NVMe formatting script and node-bootstrap DaemonSet. Verify instance health and NVMe mount.
3) Deploy serving runtime with single model; run sample latency tests and compare to expected p95.
4) Enable dynamic batching with conservative window, monitor cost/latency in first 48 hours.
5) Run disaster recovery test: restore model artifacts from S3 snapshot to on-prem NFS and run a local inference smoke test.

Notes for Solutions Eng follow-up (internal):
- Need to prepare a micro-eval for Evergreen's top 20 prompts and add into Redwood Optimize comparative workflow (quant vs non-quant).
- Prepare a small Terraform migration utility and a playbook we can hand to Evergreen infra with explicit CLI commands and rollback steps.
- Create a hardened TF variable set for GovCloud and document differences in Confluence page: Evergreen-Bank-Reqs-2024.

Next steps (owner: Priya Kapoor):
- Schedule 60-minute tech discovery with Evergreen infra + security (target next week).
- Share this draft with Marcus/Evelyn for module compatibility review and mark RFC for TF changes.
- Build quick eval harness and run baseline with sample prompts once discovery produces traffic numbers.

Appendix (quick estimator notes):
- Baseline tokens: assume avg 120 tokens per request, 2 requests per second per active user during peak; target 500 concurrent users for initial prod -> approx 120k tokens/s, shard across 10 A100 nodes with batching. This is rough — will refine after traffic profile is provided.

End of draft.
